topic: Citra Mosaic Simcoe Loral Sabro Talus Ekuanot Pahto licensed growers
finding: No licensed or propagation grower list was found. Yakima Chief Ranches says it manages Simcoe, Citra, Mosaic and Loral through its Footprints program, and the Hop Breeding Company is a joint venture of John I. Haas Inc. and Yakima Chief Ranches. The one farm level data point is Simcoe grown at Perrault Farms in 2017. The Hop Breeding Company member farms named in the owner brief (CLS, Carpenter, Perrault, Roy) are not confirmed as members by any retrieved source; Carpenter and Perrault are named as Yakima Chief Ranches founding families.

yakimachief.com returned HTTP 429 with a Vercel security checkpoint for every page tried, so the 15 owner farm roster, per farm varieties and the Cryo or lupulin processing description could not be read. Names come only from search result summaries and two 2019 articles on the four additions. The grower page and the Yakima Chief Ranches page should be re-read when access is available.

Haas history page says the Hop Breeding Company was formed by Haas and Select Botanicals LLC; other sources say Haas and Yakima Chief Ranches. A search result summary says Select Botanicals Group reverted to the name Yakima Chief Ranches in August 2018. No farm level propagation source for Citra or Mosaic was found.

The only licensed grower named is CLS Farms (2022, Sultana, Lotus, Calypso, Altus). The announcement does not name other licensed growers. No page listing Hopsteiner farms was found: hopsteiner.com/hop-farms returned 404 and its grower material sits behind a portal.

Indie Hops publishes a grower list: F & B Farms and Nursery, Fobert Farms, BC Hop Farms, B & D Hop Farms, Sodbuster Farms, Crosby Hop Farm, and Roy Farms (licensed to grow, process and sell). Goschie Farms and Coleman Agriculture are named as Indie Hops growers of multiple public varieties and are not stated to grow Strata.
CLS Farms' own site names these as its proprietary varieties. No licensed grower list for them was found.
The NASS table prints the designation VGXP01. The tie to Virgil Gamache Farms is from a search result summary only; no licensing list was found.
Gooding Farms' own site names Idaho Gem Brand 2012G01 Variety. No other grower is named.

No source gives a complete grower list or a per state grower count. USDA NASS covers only Idaho, Oregon and Washington and its December 2025 report gives acreage and production, not grower counts. A trade newsletter says the Pacific Northwest had about 70 hop farms in 2023 (anecdotal). The Oregon Encyclopedia says fewer than 30 families grow hops commercially in Oregon. Hop Growers of Michigan says more than 20 growers statewide; 25 Michigan names are recorded here. A Wisconsin source says about 100 producers; none are named here. This file records 68 farm rows (Washington 19, Oregon 12, Idaho 2, Michigan 25, Colorado 5, Minnesota 1, state unstated 4), so Washington is far below the roughly 70 Pacific Northwest farms and the Washington Hop Commission member list (not public in any source found) is the main gap.

topic: Oregon Hop Commission and Idaho Hop Commission rosters
finding: No public member list found for either commission. The Idaho Hop Commission page was located but its roster was not opened.

No named commercial farm could be sourced in New York, Wisconsin or California. Hop Growers of New York (hopgrowersofnewyork.com) did not resolve. The Wisconsin Hop Exchange site points to a Grower Map page that was not opened. A Vermont farm name appeared in a search summary without a retrievable source and was left out. 16 Quartz Hop Farm in the Hop Growers of America directory may be in California.

elkmountainfarms.com did not resolve. Ownership by Anheuser-Busch and the Bonners Ferry location come from a search result summary of an Edible Idaho article that could not be fetched (certificate mismatch).
